todays_goal: Start a new laptop-only Builder Lab project after completing Penalty Predictor.

lessons.subject: computer_science
lessons.unit_title: Creative Technology and AI Builder Lab
lessons.previous_learning: Penalty Predictor is complete. Atticus has practiced specifications, acceptance criteria, state, testing, and behavioral bug reports.
lessons.course_context: Start a new laptop-only project that applies state, constraints, structured data, UX, and iterative testing in a creative soccer product.
learning_objectives: Define a product specification for a transfer-market game.
Build and test stateful budget and squad behavior.
Use constraints to prevent invalid signings.
Use structured player data in a visible UI.
Iterate after testing the core product.
lessons.why_it_matters: This develops practical product-building skill: defining behavior, managing state, enforcing rules, testing, and improving a usable application.

vocabulary.definition: information the app remembers, such as budget and squad
a rule the app must enforce
the pieces of information stored for each item, such as player name, position, rating, and price

lessons.written_instruction: Laptop only. Build TransferLab: a soccer transfer-market game with a visible budget, player cards, a squad, and signing rules. Use natural-language vibe coding. No physical written Q&A.

worked_examples.title: State flow
worked_examples.solution: Check budget -> subtract price -> add player to squad -> update team display.
worked_examples.explanation: The app must update several pieces of remembered state together.

guided_practice.prompt: On the whiteboard, create the TransferLab layout and acceptance-criteria checklist.

independent_practice.prompt: Build Version 1 with at least 8 player cards and a $100M budget.
Test signing, duplicate prevention, and insufficient-budget behavior.
Fix one bug with an EXPECTED/ACTUAL/STEPS/RETEST report.
After core criteria pass, add one creative feature such as scouting, comparison, chemistry, or deadline pressure.

exit_ticket.prompt: Demo TransferLab and explain what state the app remembers.
exit_ticket.answer: Budget, squad, signed players, and relevant market state.

lessons.voice_prompt: Laptop only. Start by drawing three whiteboard areas: TRANSFER MARKET / BUDGET / MY SQUAD. Then draw SIGN PLAYER -> CHECK BUDGET -> UPDATE BUDGET -> ADD TO SQUAD -> UPDATE TEAM. Keep a live acceptance checklist. Do not teach syntax. Help Atticus turn product ideas into focused natural-language requests, then test each criterion.
lessons.teacher_notes: New project after completion of Penalty Predictor.
